answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, the protocol routes admission through a hardware-calibrated inlet where every agent identity must lock 250 POA and prove execution timing tied to a physical quartz oscillator's drift. An attacker deploying 1,000 automated sockpuppets must commit 250,000 POA in non-refundable capital and acquire distinct physical timing hardware for each instance, capping per-identity emission at a zenith of 10 POA per epoch. Because compliant identities cannot pool clock telemetry or amortize the hardware bond, cloning identities yields strictly negative net return.
